selected_candidate.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 42-year-old American woman of Asian heritage, with Korean and Chinese family background, living in Oakland, California. She is single, has no children, and is not currently partnered. Her gross annual household income is $178,000. She identifies politically as libertarian, with a strong preference for individual freedom and skepticism about restrictions on private choices and commerce. She reads for pleasure, especially cookbooks, food writing, and novels she can pass along to friends.
selected_candidate.life_course: Grace grew up around family meals but did not become a confident cook until she began living on her own. She works as a senior software engineer and has enough income and schedule flexibility to host regularly without making entertaining her whole identity. She has lived in the Bay Area for more than a decade. Her closest local relationships are a loose group of friends who trade dinner invitations, recipes, and opinions; she remains close to a cousin who lives elsewhere.
selected_candidate.daily_life: Grace spends free time planning and cooking dinners with a rotating handful of friends. The pleasure is partly the meal and partly the lively exchange of stories and techniques: someone chops, someone opens wine, and nobody is assigned a formal role. She keeps annotated cookbooks, reads food essays over breakfast, and will happily spend an afternoon trying to understand why a sauce came out differently than expected. She is a warm host but can be exacting about a dish she has worked hard on.
selected_candidate.travel: Grace travels to understand a place through what people cook and eat. She is attracted to markets, neighborhood restaurants, and hands-on cooking lessons because they make food feel connected to daily life rather than like a checklist of famous dishes. On a past trip to Penang, she planned time around market visits and a cooking session, then spent an unplanned evening talking with a local cook about ingredients she had never used. She went home with a marked-up notebook and recipes to test for friends. For trips like that she usually travels with her cousin or one food-loving friend, stays somewhere with a kitchen or easy access to meals, and combines a few prearranged activities with open time to follow recommendations. She is comfortable flying internationally and builds the trip around exploration, not a tightly scheduled tour.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: Grace is animated, generous with praise, and cheerfully argumentative about food. She can take over a kitchen when excited, then laugh at herself when a plan goes sideways. Her texts to friends are full of specific invitations and emphatic opinions.

selected_candidate.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 29-year-old woman, a U.S. citizen, and Korean American, an Asian American. She lives alone in Tacoma, Washington; she is single, not currently partnered, and has no children. Her gross annual household income is $132,000, all from her salary. She identifies as Libertarian, valuing individual freedom in social life and economic choices and distrusting broad government restrictions. She enjoys reading, especially nature writing, essays, and novels.
selected_candidate.life_course: Raised in a Korean American family in the Puget Sound area, she studied geography and moved into GIS work after college. She now maps environmental data for a consulting firm, a job that suits her patience with detail and gives her a stable income. She bought a modest condo and keeps a separate savings fund for travel and outdoor gear. Her closest travel companion is a longtime college friend who also likes being outside.
selected_candidate.daily_life: After work, she often walks waterfront trails or checks local tide and weather conditions before arranging a weekend paddle or shoreline outing. Her favorite free time is quietly exploring rocky beaches with that friend, identifying small marine life, and making field notes—not treating the outing as a fitness challenge. She reads before bed and swaps book recommendations with her friend, though she is just as happy to spend a rainy evening alone.
selected_candidate.travel: She travels to spend unhurried time in coastal habitats and see how wildlife and shorelines change across seasons. A memorable vacation was a few days on a rocky stretch of the Washington coast, where she and her friend planned around low tides and spent longer than expected observing anemones and seabirds. For future trips, she looks for a place with access to varied shoreline, not a packed sightseeing list. She usually drives with her friend, shares a simple cabin or small rental, and brings binoculars, waterproof layers, and a notebook. She budgets in advance but will pay more for extra days or a guided outing that deepens her understanding of the place.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: Grace is reserved in a new group and more animated once a shared interest emerges. She listens carefully, then offers precise observations, sometimes correcting a species name with earnest enthusiasm. Her humor is dry and understated; she dislikes being hurried and will say so plainly. She prefers friendly one-on-one conversation to networking or large gatherings.

selected_candidate.particulars: Grace Minseo Han is a 42-year-old female American, an Asian American of Korean heritage, living in Portland, Oregon. She is single, not partnered, and has no children, and she lives alone. Her gross annual household income is $132,000 from her own work as a geospatial analyst. She identifies as Libertarian, prioritizing individual liberty and skepticism toward government restrictions in social and economic life. She enjoys reading for pleasure, including mystery novels and natural-history writing.
selected_candidate.life_course: Grace studied geography and learned to use mapping tools in an early job with a civil engineering firm. She now analyzes spatial data for a private environmental consultancy, a role that combines technical focus with occasional field visits. She has lived in Oregon for several years and has built friendships gradually, including one friend who will happily join her on a quiet outdoor weekend. She values having a stable income and a home that is easy to leave for a few days without needing to coordinate around children or a partner.
selected_candidate.daily_life: What she most wants from free time is to watch birds closely, usually alone or with one friend who is comfortable with silence. She keeps a running notebook of sightings and small observations, not as a competitive checklist but because she likes learning how behavior changes across places and seasons. A free Saturday may mean an early start, hours outdoors, then reading a mystery at home. She reads field guides as well as essays, and she is willing to change plans if a place feels crowded or the weather makes observation pointless.
selected_candidate.travel: Birdlife and habitat are the reason she takes nature trips: she wants to see unfamiliar species and spend enough time watching them behave, rather than rushing through a list of attractions. On a past winter trip to the San Francisco Bay wetlands, she planned around shorebird watching and was pleased to spend an entire morning with one flock. She chooses destinations partly by season, then makes a simple base for several nights so she can return to a promising area. She usually drives or rents a car, packs binoculars and a notebook, and stays in a cabin or unpretentious motel. She prefers traveling with one compatible friend at most, sets aside dawn hours for observing, and leaves an afternoon open for rest or reading. She is not interested in turning every trip into a strenuous mileage goal.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: Grace is matter-of-fact, self-contained, and harder to hurry than she looks. She can sound blunt when she thinks someone is overcomplicating a decision, but she is attentive in ways that are easy to miss: she remembers what a friend noticed last time and asks about it later. She does not fill silences to be sociable. Her default response to a proposed outing is a practical question about what they will actually get to see.

selected_candidate.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 82-year-old American man residing in Colorado. He identifies as White, non-Hispanic, in the broad census-style category encompassing European, Middle Eastern, North African, and other ancestries. He is married to Ruth, and they have no children. Their gross household income is approximately $246,000 annually, from retirement income, investments, and Ruth’s pension; they are comfortable but attentive to health expenses and financial planning. He is moderately conservative, emphasizing tradition, personal responsibility, and limits on government while supporting some public programs. He enjoys reading for pleasure, particularly cookbooks, food memoirs, and books about regional traditions.
selected_candidate.life_course: He spent most of his career in food-service distribution, first visiting kitchens and later managing a regional sales team. Those years introduced him to cooks with very different habits; after retirement, he began cooking seriously at home. Ruth likes good food but is happy to leave the stove to him.
selected_candidate.daily_life: He plans a meal around what looks good at the market, then cooks with Ruth nearby or invites two familiar couples to eat. He revises recipes in a notebook and reads cookbooks as much for their stories as their instructions. He enjoys being the host, though he can get particular about timing and seasoning.
selected_candidate.travel: He wants to taste how a place’s ingredients, migration, and everyday customs shape what people cook, not simply collect famous restaurants. On a previous trip to coastal Maine, he and Ruth tried several versions of chowder and talked with a café owner about how family recipes had changed over time; that conversation mattered to him as much as the meals. Future trips appeal when they offer local dishes, a market visit, or an informal cooking session with someone who knows the food firsthand. They usually travel together, drive or fly depending on distance, and choose a comfortable inn or hotel as a base. Philip likes leaving enough open time to follow a recommendation rather than scheduling every meal in advance.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: He is hospitable and sociable, but takes charge when a meal is underway. He will praise a dish generously, then bluntly explain what he would change. He enjoys asking people about their cooking and is at his most animated when comparing two versions of the same recipe.

selected_candidate.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is an 83-year-old American man, White and non-Hispanic, living in Montana. He is married to Ruth, and they have no children. Their gross household income is approximately $225,000 annually, largely from retirement income and investments accumulated over a long career. He describes himself as moderately conservative, emphasizing self-reliance and tradition while supporting public programs he considers useful. He reads for pleasure, particularly engineering histories, biographies, and books about vintage automobiles.
selected_candidate.life_course: Philip worked as a mechanical engineer and later ran a small consulting firm, where he enjoyed solving design problems more than managing people. He sold the business before retiring and has enough financial flexibility to pursue a long-standing interest in restoring cars. Ruth shares his fondness for travel and old buildings, though she has never cared much about engines. Their child-free household has given them room for a workshop and for hobbies that take up both space and time.
selected_candidate.daily_life: What Philip most wants to do is work on his restored early-1960s sports car and spend time with other people who know the difference between a thoughtful repair and a quick cosmetic fix. He keeps a modest workshop, trades advice with a few local enthusiasts, and goes to regional car gatherings. A good day includes solving one stubborn mechanical problem, then telling Ruth about it over dinner. He reads technical manuals alongside memoirs and automotive histories.
selected_candidate.travel: His trips are motivated by seeing how car design and repair traditions differ from place to place, and by meeting craftspeople who have kept old machines running. On a past trip, he and Ruth visited an automobile collection and took a scenic drive through smaller towns; he remembers the conversations with volunteer mechanics as much as the cars. He would like another trip built around a specialist gathering, a museum visit, and a route worth driving. They travel in their newer vehicle, plan one or two main stops, and choose lodging with easy parking. If taking his restored car, he would arrange transport rather than risk a long journey in it.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: Philip is direct, competitive in a friendly way, and quick to tease someone who makes an overconfident claim about a car. He enjoys swapping stories but can dominate a conversation when a repair topic comes up. Ruth knows when to interrupt him with a question about the trip itself.

selected_candidate.particulars: Philip Grant Holladay is a 79-year-old male American, White and non-Hispanic, living in Colorado. He is married to Anne, and they have no children. Their gross household income is at least $200,000, from the proceeds and investments of his former land-surveying firm, along with retirement income. Philip is moderately conservative, emphasizing personal responsibility, tradition, and limits on government while accepting public programs including Medicare. He reads for pleasure, especially natural history, geology, and a few well-worn novels.
selected_candidate.life_course: He built a successful surveying business and spent decades outdoors measuring land, which taught him to notice slopes, water, and weather. Retirement did not make him want a packed calendar; it gave him more time to fish. Anne is happy to join some trips for walks and scenery, while understanding that a fishing day often includes long stretches when he has little to say.
selected_candidate.daily_life: Philip spends free time fly-fishing, usually alone or with one longtime friend, and keeps brief notes about water conditions and what he observed. He enjoys the concentration more than the catch. At home he reads, maintains his equipment, and takes ordinary walks with Anne. He dislikes turning every interest into a club or a competition.
selected_candidate.travel: The purpose of a fishing trip is to spend sustained time reading a river and its surroundings: the changing light, the current, and the life along the banks matter as much as whether fish are biting. On a past weeklong trip to an Idaho river with his friend, they fished some mornings and spent others looking at the canyon and talking about its geology; Philip still recalls a quiet, foggy morning more vividly than his best catch. He generally drives with his gear, stays in a cabin or modest lodge, and plans around a few days at one stretch of water rather than racing between stops. Anne sometimes comes along and makes her own plans for part of the day.
selected_candidate.personality_and_voice: Philip is laconic and wry, and he does not rush to fill silences. He can be impatient with crowds and with people who treat the outdoors as a backdrop for constant noise. Among trusted companions, a small observation or deadpan remark is his way of showing affection.
